Example: 2028-05-20T16:22:14Z and 2028-05-21T03:08:50Z — both show an upstream timeout in our gateway with an empty body returned from the service call. We've attached a short screen capture and a trimmed log extract showing the request IDs.

What we need: an initial triage and confirmation whether this looks like a platform-side issue or something in our request path. This has customer-facing impact, so any ETA for a deep look would be appreciated.

Subject: Re: Intermittent request timeouts — initial triage notes (internal)

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal note while I dig in. I pulled platform ingress logs and our downstream worker traces for the times cited. Findings so far:

- No 5xx from Redwood application layer for those exact request IDs. The path from our routing proxy to the model runner shows normal handoffs.
- There are a handful of long-tail token generation latencies (~>12s) during the 2028-05-20 16:20–16:30Z window, but no generator OOMs or kernel errors.
- The HorizonPay logs show immediate client-side gateway timeouts returned to the caller; their gateway appears to be closing the connection before the full model response arrives in several cases.

Requesting HorizonPay: full request headers and confirmation of any proxy timeouts or retries on their side. Also recommending they re-play a failing request with a longer client timeout (60s) so we can capture an end-to-end trace.

I'll attach a small snippet of our relevant ingress trace here (redwood-triage-note-snippet.txt). If Marissa agrees, we can mark this as 'no platform error found — needs client timeout adjustment' but open an ops action to monitor for recurrence.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent request timeouts impacting HorizonPay — follow-up & closure

Hi Devon — thanks for the additional logs and patience while we investigated. Summary of our triage and next steps: 

Summary:
- We reviewed Redwood ingress traces, model runner metrics, and the artifacts you provided for the 2028-05-20 16:22 UTC window.
- We do not see any platform-side errors (5xx) or process crashes tied to your request IDs. Model runners returned tokens in all traced sessions; a small percentage showed extended generation latency (long-tail), but not failures.
- HorizonPay's gateway (Kong) is set to a 30s proxy_read_timeout and there are client retries that correlate with observed empty-body handoffs. This pattern is consistent with the gateway closing the connection before our full response is streamed back in some requests.

Outcome & recommendation:
- Conclusion: No evidence of a Redwood infrastructure or model failure causing the reported empty responses. The most likely root cause is client-side/proxy timeout behavior combined with long-tail token-generation latency in a small subset of requests.
- Suggested mitigations for HorizonPay: increase proxy_read_timeout to 60s for the affected route, enable streaming/early-flush for large prompt cases, and add idempotency keys to suppress duplicate processing on retries.
- We're happy to run a joint live debug session to reproduce with extended timeouts and capture a full end-to-end trace. If you'd like that, propose a 1-hour window and we'll bring an SRE and a Runtime engineer.

I've attached our triage notes (redwood-triage-notes-HP-9835.pdf) and linked the HubSpot ticket for tracking. If you prefer we can also open a watch/alert so we proactively notify you if similar long-tail latencies are observed.

Closing note: Given our findings, we'll close this as 'no platform error found' for now. Please reopen the ticket if you hit repeatable failures after applying the suggested mitigations — we'll prioritize a joint session.

Best regards,
